subject: Hosted API expansion pricing — commit tiers & per-token discounts
messages:
From: Kelly Moore <kelly.moore@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing for expansion use cases / per-token discounts

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked good and the team is excited to move forward. We're finalizing an internal business case for two additional workloads that would be new to the contract: automated patient intake summaries (higher throughput, small prompts) and a clinical decision-support reranking service (lower throughput, longer context).

Before we pull procurement in, can you confirm:
- How per-token volume discounts apply across multiple products under one account (do commits aggregate across teams/products?)
- Whether we can phase in additional commit tiers over time (e.g., Q2 initial incremental commit, larger Q4 expansion) without losing earlier pricing tiers:
  - If we start with a $25k/month equivalent commit for Q2 and add another $75k/month in Q4, what effective per-token rates do we land at and when do they apply?
- Any minimums or carve-outs for embeddings vs. chat/generation tokens (we expect embeddings-heavy usage for search indices).

Procurement also asked for a short pricing table and an SLA summary to attach to their packet — if you can send a one-pager and a simple tier table that maps committed spend to per-token unit pricing, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Kelly
Kelly Moore
Director, Platform Engineering
Atlas Health

[Attachment: requirements_matrix.csv (referenced)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Moore <kelly.moore@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing for expansion use cases / per-token discounts

Hi Kelly — great to hear the team found the demo useful. Short answers up front, then details below: yes, commits aggregate across products under the same account; you can phase in commits and keep earlier tiers; embeddings are priced differently (lower per-unit cost after commit thresholds). I'm attaching a proposed tier table and a one-page SLA digest.

Key points:
- Aggregation: Commits are account-level. All attached projects under Atlas Health will count toward the same commit pool. This means you can have spikes in one product consume credit from the shared commit.
- Phasing: We support incremental commits. Pricing is evaluated at month-end against total committed spend. Example: start $25k/mo (Q2), add $75k/mo in Q4 — once the Q4 commit becomes active (billing cycle), your pricing tier will be recalculated using the current 3-month rolling committed volume for smoothing; you won't retroactively lose the Q2 pricing for months already billed.
- Effective rates: See attached Proposed_Tier_Table.xlsx for concrete per-token numbers across typical generation/chat and embedding units. As an illustrative example (not final):
  - <$50k/mo: $0.0008/token gen; $0.0002/token embed
  - $50k–$150k/mo: $0.0005/token gen; $0.00015/token embed
  - >$150k/mo: $0.00035/token gen; $0.00010/token embed

Operational notes:
- Commit term: monthly (auto-renews) under the hosted API. We can put a 3- or 12-month commitment term in the SOW if Procurement prefers.
- Change window: additions to commit take effect at the start of the next billing cycle unless you request an immediate pro-rated activation.
- Carve-outs: we can exclude any development / staging projects from counting toward billing via a tagging policy — good for pilot teams.

Next steps from our side:
1) Connor will confirm any infra constraints for large embedding writes and propose a batching recommendation.
2) I'll draft a short SOW language for phased commits and the pricing table for Procurement.

Attaching: Proposed_Tier_Table.xlsx, Redwood_SLA_Digest.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0184

[Attachment: Proposed_Tier_Table.xlsx]
[Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Digest.pdf]
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Moore <kelly.moore@atlashealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing for expansion use cases / per-token discounts

Thanks — quick technical note on the embedding workload so your engineers have visibility: 

- If Atlas writes large initial indexes (hundreds of millions of tokens), we recommend bulk ingest windows using our batch ingestion endpoint and temporary caching to reduce KV cache thrash. That will substantially lower observed per-token latency and reduce peak cost.
- For real-time scoring/reranking, keep context windows to the smallest sensible size and cache recent keys. That pattern keeps latency predictable and helps you hit the higher discount tiers because fewer tokens are spent per inference.

I can put together an expected monthly token burn estimate for both workloads if you share expected daily throughput and average context lengths. That helps Marissa build the precise pricing scenario for Q2->Q4 phasing.

—Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Inline: short code snippet for batch ingestion omitted]
From: Kelly Moore <kelly.moore@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing for expansion use cases / per-token discounts

Marissa / Connor — thanks, that helps. Quick answers to help you model:
- Patient intake summaries: expect ~1.2M gen tokens/day when at scale (peak months), avg prompt+response = 480 tokens.
- Reranking: expect ~150k embed tokens/day initially, with embeddings batch writes of ~30M tokens for initial indexing (one-time).
- We want a pricing path that keeps per-token cost predictable for budgeting — Procurement leans toward a 12-month SOW with quarterly review points.

Can you model two scenarios in the table:
A) Conservative: start $25k/mo for 90 days, then add $75k/mo at month 4
B) Aggressive: start $50k/mo and add $100k/mo at month 7

Procurement also asked whether Redwood offers any one-time credits for migration costs (indexing, dedicated migration support). If that's possible, include it as a negotiable line item.

Best,
Kelly
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Moore <kelly.moore@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing for expansion use cases / per-token discounts

Kelly — appreciate the numbers. We're happy to model both scenarios and we can offer a migration credit as part of the initial commit (common for larger deals). High-level proposal: 

- Migration credit: one-time $10k professional-services credit applied during the first billing cycle for indexing/migration support (negotiable).
- Scenario A (conservative):
  - Months 1–3: $25k/mo commit -> effective blended rate (generation) $0.0008/token
  - Month 4 onward (after adding $75k/mo): new tier applied, blended effective generation rate ~ $0.00045/token (see attached modeling)
- Scenario B (aggressive):
  - Start $50k/mo -> immediate move into mid-tier pricing; after adding $100k/mo in month 7 you would hit top-tier discounts and embedding rates improve materially (down to ~$0.00010/token embed).

We generally compute effective rates on a rolling basis and will show month-by-month cashflow and token economics in the modeled spreadsheet. I'll attach the two modeled sheets and draft SOW language that captures: aggregation, phasing mechanics, migration credit, carve-outs for dev/staging, and a standard 30-day change window.

Vivek — looping you in for approval on the migration credit and to confirm whether we want to set an upper bound on promotional discounts for this enterprise account.

—Marissa
